transcript_text:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recordings: cloud.fireflies.ai/rec/ff_20250715_acme_001
Attendees: Alex Ramirez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions); Michael Chen (CTO, Acme Modernization Co.), Sahana Rao (Platform Eng), Jorge Velasquez (Security Lead), Emma Li (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Quick intro to Redwood hosted API and options for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Customer is evaluating tradeoffs: time-to-first-token, security controls (SAML/KMS), cost vs latency, and path to Dedicated reserved capacity.
- Agreed to send security docs, provision free credits, run a latency/cost benchmark session, and reconvene to discuss Dedicated pricing.

Topics: quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token, security (SOC2/SAML/KMS), dedicated vs hosted, pilot benchmarking

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we good to record?
[00:05] Michael (Acme CTO): Yes that's fine, go ahead. Thanks Alex.
[00:09] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, I'm Priya, I'm the solutions engineer who'll help with the benching and the quickstart. We'll keep it high level for the first 10 and then dig into infra if you want.
[00:20] Sahana (Acme): Sounds good, our main ask is: we need something we can ship into production in 2-3 months, but security is non-negotiable.
[00:27] Jorge (Security): Yep, SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, kms integration, and data residency questions. We'll need those answered before a pilot.
[00:35] Alex: Totally understood. Quick run-through: Redwood has the hosted API which is the fastest to get started — free credits, self-serve console, SDKs — so time-to-first-token is usually minutes to hours. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools we can provision when you need predictable throughput and isolation, and Private is our VPC/on-prem option for regulated workloads.
[00:52] Michael: When you say "minutes to hours" what's the typical path? I mean from sign-up to actually calling the API from our app.
[00:58] Priya: If you sign up and spin up a project, you get sample keys, our SDK, and a quickstart example that hits a small model. So if you copy-paste the node/python snippet you can be calling in under 15 minutes for basic functionality. Then you swap in your prompt set and scale.
[01:15] Emma (Product): Do you also have a hosted playground for prompt testing?
[01:18] Alex: Yep, Console has a playground and we keep token cost estimates and latency graphs for the model catalog.
[01:25] Sahana: Our platform team is worried about bursty traffic — how does Redwood handle autoscaling?
[01:31] Priya: For hosted, it's handled by our control plane with autoscaling policies, and we provide guidance on batching and cache. For Dedicated you can set reserved capacity and burst options; we can also put A/B routing rules.
[01:42] Sahana: How much work is it to move from hosted to Dedicated later? We want a low-friction path so we don't re-architect.
[01:48] Alex: The API surface is identical — you pin model versions, rollout policies — so from code perspective it's mostly a config change. There are infra steps for Dedicated (provisioning GPUs, subnet/network setup) but it's designed to be seamless.
[01:58] Jorge: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys or HSM? We have a compliance requirement for CMEK.
[02:03] Priya: Yes, we support KMS integrations and can enable CMEK for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted we support envelope encryption and dedicated configs for enterprise customers; I'll attach the exact docs.
[02:15] Michael: Cost — curious how you help customers estimate token unit economics.
[02:19] Alex: We have Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization, model suggestions) and the Console shows per-token and inference cost breakdowns. For benchmarking we run a perf pass with your prompts and payloads, and return cost per 1k tokens and latency P50/P90.
[02:32] Emma: Can you run benchmarks with our prompt set? We have a mix of short completions and multi-turn chat.
[02:37] Priya: Absolutely. If you share the top-20 most used prompts and expected payload sizes, we can run a simulated workload and provide the numbers.
[02:44] Michael: About data retention — will prompt history be stored? We want ephemeral flows for some endpoints.
[02:49] Alex: You can configure retention policies and disable logging on per-route basis for sensitive routes. Private deployments give you the most control.
[02:56] Jorge: Any independent audits? SOC2? ISO?
[02:59] Alex: We are SOC2 Type II — I'll send the certs and the security pack.
[03:05] Sahana: On network setup for Dedicated, do you support VPC peering or private link?
[03:09] Priya: Both — VPC peering and PrivateLink patterns are supported depending on cloud provider. For Private on-prem we'll go through air-gapped options.
[03:16] Michael: Let's talk about latency — our product requires P50 < 150ms for short prompts. Is that realistic on hosted?
[03:24] Priya: For small models and optimized kernels, hosted can hit <150ms P50 for single-token generation on optimized hardware in nearby regions. For consistent low tail latency at scale, many customers use Dedicated where you control pool sizing and reduce noisy neighbor effects.
[03:39] Michael: So if we want to validate, you recommend a bench on hosted first and then consider Dedicated if tail latency or throughput demands it?
[03:46] Priya: Exactly. Hosted is easiest for time-to-first-token; if the bench shows you need tighter SLOs, we can work the Dedicated path.
[03:52] Emma: You mentioned quantization — do you do model quantization automatically?
[03:56] Alex: We provide quantization profiles and suggestions in Redwood Optimize — some quantizations are model-dependent and we can recommend appropriate tradeoffs for quality vs cost.
[04:05] Sahana: For onboarding, what's the minimal engineering effort? One engineer or a team?
[04:09] Alex: Many teams get started with a single SWE and a product owner — they'd use the quickstart, sample SDKs, and console. For pilot to production, Platform/Infra involvement is needed for Dedicated/Private.
[04:20] Michael: Ok that sounds reasonable. On the free credits — how much and what's the cap?
[04:24] Alex: For trials we typically provide a set of free credits geared to validate common flows — enough to run bench scenarios across a few models. I'll provision a sandbox with credits and share the link.
[04:32] Jorge: On SSO — do you support SAML/SCIM for user provisioning?
[04:36] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM-based group provisioning for enterprise orgs. I'll attach the exact IdP instructions.
[04:42] Michael: Any gotchas around token rotation? We want short-lived keys and automatic rotation.
[04:47] Alex: We support short-lived tokens and recommend using our SDK for rotation flows; we also support API key rotation via the Console and have examples in the quickstart.
[04:55] Sahana: For the bench, we'd like to test both short completions and multi-turn chat with KV cache behavior — is that in scope?
[05:02] Priya: Definitely. We'll simulate sessions, measure P50/P90/P99 and note KV cache hit/miss to estimate cost impact. Also note sometimes the transcript: people call it K V cash — we actually mean KV cache.
[05:14] Emma: Any reference customers who've done a similar migration?
[05:17] Alex: Yes, a financial data platform recently moved from hosted to Dedicated; they provided a case study — I'll include a short reference.
[05:23] Michael: On pricing — is Dedicated an annual commitment?
[05:26] Alex: Typically yes, Reserved capacity has monthly/annual commit options; we can do shorter pilots but pricing is different. We'll share rough numbers after the bench.
[05:35] Sahana: Is there an easy way to simulate concurrency to see tail latency?
[05:38] Priya: We have a load harness we run in our env against your sandbox; we can also share the harness if you'd like to run locally.
[05:45] Michael: Great. For our evaluation criteria — security, predictable latency, cost — can you help us map metrics to pass/fail?
[05:52] Alex: Yes — we'll produce a bench report with P50/P90/P99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and error rates; tie that back to your pass/fail thresholds.
[05:59] Jorge: A practical Q: for data residency, can hosted be configured to keep data in EU only?
[06:04] Priya: We have region controls for hosted customers; for strict residency Private is the recommended path. We'll include region mapping in the docs.
[06:12] Emma: Okay, so immediate asks: security docs, sandbox with credits, quickstart links, and a bench session.
[06:18] Alex: Yep — that's the plan. Anything else?
[06:21] Michael: Timeline: we'd like bench results in two weeks if possible.
[06:25] Priya: That should be doable once we have the prompt set and expected QPS.
[06:29] Michael: Final question — how do you handle model updates and rollouts? We don't want surprises when a model changes.
[06:35] Alex: Console has model versioning, canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback policies. You pin a model version per route if you want strict control.
[06:44] Speaker 1: (inaudible) quick question about the SDK language support.
[06:47] Alex: We have official SDKs for Python, Node, and a community SDK for Go; other languages use REST.
[06:53] Emma: Any limits on prompt size?
[06:55] Priya: Limits depend on model and config; we'll recommend a model and max sequence length based on your prompt mix.
[07:02] Michael: Ok great. That covers my list.
[07:05] Alex: Recap of next steps: I'll send SOC2 and security pack, Priya will provision a sandbox project with free credits and the quickstart, you (Michael/Sahana) will share the prompt set and expected traffic, we run a bench and come back with results and recommended path (hosted -> Dedicated if needed).
[07:23] Sahana: Sounds good.
[07:25] Jorge: One last note — can you include legal contacts for data processing addendum and standard contractual clauses?
[07:30] Alex: Yes — I'll include legal contacts and the DPA template.
[07:33] Michael: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[07:36] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up via email with attachments and a calendar invite for the bench.
[07:40] (call ends)
